items.title: Bare-metal 74 KB hypervisor puts a 2B LLM in Ring -1 to catch Linux kernel panics and live-patch guest RAM
items.summary: Part 4 of the llm.asm project runs a MiniCPM5-2B engine in a tiny Type-1 hypervisor below Linux; when the guest hits a fatal Ring 0 fault the model inspects the faulting bytes and chooses to patch, pass the fault to Linux, or halt, so the demo kernel keeps running without a reboot. Source, GRPO training and eval scripts are MIT.

doubt.pushback: Several repliers argue that patching over a panic can hide corruption or an intrusion and that halting is safer; the author replies the model can choose PASS_TO_LINUX or HALT_FOR_DUMP and the eval showed zero dangerous patches, but it is one author's test on injected faults.

reception.summary: Mostly amazement; the substantive replies question whether surviving a kernel fault is desirable versus failing safe, and the author explains the patch, pass and halt choices.

items.title: OpenCode Rune early dev build: native Rust desktop app with no Electron
items.summary: OpenCode opened an early build of Rune, its next desktop client for the OpenCode coding agent, built on its own native app framework instead of Electron, with embeddable session crates. MIT licensed.

doubt.pushback: Early testers note Chromium still downloads the first time the built-in browser is used, one Fedora user saw only 10 to 20 percent lower resource use, and one profiler says it still trails native SwiftUI apps.

reception.summary: Users welcome dropping Electron because agent sessions already strain RAM; a few who tried it report modest gains and missing polish such as Ctrl+Enter to send.

items.title: SGLang Omni turns speech into a tool call, cutting first audio from 1,826 to 567 ms
items.summary: In SGLang Omni the LLM decides what to say aloud through a TTS tool call while the server decides when speech stops and tells the model how much the user actually heard, enabling full-duplex barge-in and speaking before the thought is finished; first-audio latency fell about 3x averaged over three models.

items.title: Cohere Labs releases CulturalRiddles, locally written riddles from 62 countries as a cultural-understanding benchmark
items.summary: A new open benchmark of original, culturally grounded riddles written by locals across 62 countries, with a paper and interactive results, for testing whether models understand local culture rather than just reasoning puzzles.

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini reaches 264.5 tok/s single-user and 950 tok/s at 8 users on one RTX PRO 6000 with DFlash2 drafts in vLLM
items.summary: Using Inco AI's DFlash2 block-diffusion draft model for lossless speculative decoding in vLLM, Inkling-2-Mini serving on a single RTX PRO 6000 rose 39 percent single-user and 33 percent at 8 concurrent users over the previous record; the setup was tuned with Gemini 4 Neon.

items.title: TensorFold 1.3.7 speeds Inkling 2 Mini prefill 23 percent on M5 Ultra and adds DFlash2 drafting on Metal
items.summary: The local inference runtime's new release fills 2K and 8K prompts 23 percent faster and decodes 3 to 6 percent faster on M5 Ultra with identical output tokens, fixes model loading on macOS 27.0, adds DFlash2 drafting on Metal and multi-stream drafting on CUDA, and serves Kolibri 1.1 on CUDA. A community repo packages Inkling 2 Mini on one RTX 5090 with 256k context.

items.title: Anpaure Pretrain Index estimates bits per byte for closed frontier models from API outputs
items.summary: A method to rank pretraining quality of closed models: the model must pick the real continuation of held-out text over a decoy written by a small open model, and that choice rate is calibrated against true perplexity on open models to estimate log-perplexity for API-only models.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask for error bars by holding out open-weight models whose bits per byte can be computed directly, question extrapolating from one vendor's curve, and note tokenizer and instruct-model decoy choices may bias the ranking.

reception.summary: Researchers praise the idea and note it ranks known same-base pairs together; the critical replies are about validation and extrapolation rather than the core trick.

items.title: Max Woolf: Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2 pushed his Rust libraries close to hardware limits
items.summary: A long first-hand write-up of using agentic coding models, with checks against regressions and cheating, to further optimize already-fast Rust crates, with benchmark comparisons against existing libraries such as umap-learn.
